questions.question: A classroom analog clock has the numbers 1 to 12 around the edge, and between every pair of numbers there are 4 small marks. So each small mark stands for 1 minute and each number stands for 5 minutes. Right now the hour hand is a little past the 7, and the minute hand is 2 small marks past the 4. What time is it?
questions.explain: The 4 means 20 minutes, then count on 2 more small marks: 20 + 2 = 22, and the hour hand has already passed the 7, so it is 7:22. The usual trap is stopping at the number and writing 7:20.

questions.question: On an analog clock, each number stands for 5 minutes and each of the 4 small marks between two numbers stands for 1 minute. The hour hand is between the 2 and the 3. The minute hand is 3 small marks past the 9. What time is it?
questions.explain: The 9 stands for 45 minutes, so count on 3 small marks: 45 + 3 = 48. When the hour hand sits between two numbers you always name the smaller one, so it is 2:48, not 3:48.

questions.question: An analog clock has 4 small marks between each pair of numbers, so one small mark is 1 minute and one number is 5 minutes. The hour hand is a little past the 11, and the minute hand is exactly 1 small mark past the 3. What time is it?
questions.explain: The minute hand on the 3 is quarter past, which is 15 minutes, and one more small mark makes 16, so the time is 11:16. Remember a small mark adds 1 minute, not 5.

questions.question: An analog clock has 4 small marks between each pair of numbers, so each small mark is 1 minute and each number is 5 minutes. The hour hand is almost at the 6, and the minute hand is 2 small marks before the 12. What time is it?
questions.explain: Two marks before the 12 means 60 - 2 = 58 minutes, and the hour hand has not reached the 6 yet, so it is 5:58. Two common slips are jumping the hour up to 6:58 and counting the 2 marks forwards to get 5:02.

questions.question: Maya is waiting for the ferry at Horseshoe Bay. The terminal's analog clock has its hour hand between the 9 and the 10, and its minute hand 3 small marks past the 8. What time does her digital watch show at that same moment?
questions.explain: The 8 stands for 40 minutes, plus 3 small marks makes 43, and the hour hand has not reached the 10, so it is 9:43. Reading only to the nearest 5 gives 9:40, which is 3 minutes off.

questions.question: Dev's digital clock reads 4:26 and he wants to set his analog clock to the very same time. Where should he point the minute hand?
questions.explain: The number 5 stands for 25 minutes, so 26 minutes is one small mark past the 5. Stopping exactly on the 5 shows 25 minutes, and the 2 in 26 is not a number to aim at.

questions.question: It is the afternoon. The analog clock in the Nanaimo library has its hour hand almost at the 3 and its minute hand 4 small marks before the 12. The sign at the front desk shows the same time on a 24-hour clock. What does the sign show?
questions.explain: Four marks before the 12 is 60 - 4 = 56 minutes, and the hour hand has not reached the 3, so it is 2:56 in the afternoon, written 14:56 on a 24-hour clock. Counting those 4 marks forwards by mistake gives 14:04.

questions.question: Sam is at the rink before hockey practice. The rink's analog clock has its hour hand almost at the 7 and its minute hand 1 small mark before the 9. Which sentence is true?
options: It is 6:44, one minute before quarter to 7.
questions.explain: The minute hand on the 9 is quarter to, which is 45 minutes, so one small mark before it is 44 minutes, and the hour hand is still on 6: the time is 6:44. Saying quarter to 7 rounds away that one minute.

questions.question: Jia looks at the kitchen analog clock. The minute hand is 2 small marks before the 11, and the hour hand is almost touching the 9. She writes 9:53 in her notebook. What is the correct time, and why?
options: 9:53 — the hour hand is nearest the 9
8:55 — the minute hand is nearest the 11
9:55 — the minutes should be rounded to the nearest 5
8:53 — the hour hand has not passed the 9 yet
questions.explain: Two marks before the 11 is 55 - 2 = 53 minutes, and the hour hand names the hour it has already gone past, not the one it is heading toward, so the time is 8:53. Near the end of an hour the hour hand almost touches the next number, which fools a lot of people.

questions.question: Liam's microwave shows 3:38. The analog clock on the wall above it has its hour hand between the 3 and the 4, and its minute hand 1 small mark past the 8. Which clock is ahead, and by how many minutes?
options: They show exactly the same time
questions.explain: The 8 means 40 minutes and one more small mark makes 41, so the analog clock reads 3:41, which is 3 minutes ahead of 3:38. If you read it only to the nearest 5 as 3:40, the gap looks like just 2 minutes.

questions.question: Noah reads the gym clock: the hour hand is between the 10 and the 11, and the minute hand is 2 small marks before the 4. He writes 10:22. Which sentence explains his mistake best?
options: Each small mark is 5 minutes, so 2 marks is 10 minutes and the time is 10:10, not 10:22.
He read the hour hand wrong; it is closer to the 11, so the time is 11:22, not 10:22.
He counted the 2 small marks forwards past the 4 instead of backwards; the time is 10:18.
He should round to the nearest 5 minutes, because clocks are read in fives; the time is 10:20.
questions.explain: The 4 stands for 20 minutes, and two marks before it is 20 - 2 = 18, so the clock reads 10:18. Always check which side of the number the minute hand is on before you count the small marks.

questions.question: Rina's swim lesson at the Kelowna pool starts at quarter past 4. When she walks on deck, the pool's analog clock has its hour hand a little past the 4 and its minute hand 2 small marks past the 3. How late is she?
questions.explain: The minute hand on the 3 is 15 minutes, plus 2 small marks makes 4:17, and quarter past 4 is 4:15, so she is 2 minutes late. The 17 is the minutes shown on the clock, not how late she is.
